title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding (2026, People-ops Guide)
author: Avery Chen
content:
Purpose:

This consolidated People-ops guide provides a single reference for working at Redwood: our cultural principles, role definitions and leveling rubrics, hiring and onboarding workflows, benefits and perks summary, and the most-used internal tools and access procedures. Managers should link to this page during new-hire onboarding and promotion conversations.

1) Principles and expectations

- Developer-first mindset: prioritize shipping production quality and observable outcomes.
- Ownership and documentation: all services and features must have clear owners and runbooks.
- Inclusive hiring and feedback: use structured rubrics and timely, actionable feedback.
- Continuous growth: support learning, mentoring, and transparent career progression.

Core employee expectations:
- Attend weekly team sync and monthly product demos.
- Keep Jira tickets current and link related Confluence pages.
- Participate in on-call rotations if your role requires it.

2) Roles & career ladders (summary and rubrics)

Engineering IC ladder (high level):
| Level | Title | Scope | Promotion signals |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Software Engineer I | Task-level contributions, close mentoring | Reliable completion of assigned tasks; clear, tested code |
| E2 | Software Engineer II | Owns component features and bugs | Leads feature cycles; reduces operational toil |
| E3 | Senior Engineer | Cross-component design and mentorship | Leads system designs; measurable reliability/cost improvements |
| E4 | Staff Engineer | Domain-level influence, technical leadership | Sets strategy for multiple services; published design docs |
| E5 | Principal Engineer | Company-wide technical strategy | Influences platform roadmap; long-term architecture ownership |

Management ladder (high level):
- M1 Engineering Manager: owns a team (4-8), career development, and quarterly delivery.
- M2 Senior Eng Manager: multiple teams, cross-team planning.
- M3 Director+: org-level strategy and people development.

Product, Research, and Support ladders:
- Product: PM I → PM II → Senior PM → Group PM → Director PM.
- Research/Applied ML: Research Engineer → Senior Research Engineer → Staff Researcher.
- CS & Support: CS Rep → Senior CS → Manager.

Promotion process (4-step):
1. Candidate prepares a promotion packet (1-page impact summary, 3-5 artifacts, peer feedback).
2. Manager endorsement and documented development plan.
3. Calibration review with peers and HR.
4. Decision communicated within 30 days.

Promotion signals (examples):
- Reduced MTTR for a service by X% and eliminated recurring incidents.
- Delivered a cross-team feature that improved customer latency or unit economics.
- Mentored and successfully onboarded new hires.

3) Hiring workflow & DEI practices

Standard interview loop (engineering & product):
1. Recruiter screen (30–60 min)
2. Hiring manager screen (30–60 min)
3. Technical assessment (take-home 2-4 hrs or live 60-90 min)
4. Onsite loop (3-5 interviews: coding, system design, behavioral, cross-functional)
5. Reference checks, offer, and negotiation handled by People-ops

Timing expectations:
- Target time-to-offer: 3 weeks from first screen for active roles.
- Interview feedback required within 48 hours of each interview.

DEI & structured interviewing best practices:
- Use calibrated rubrics and shared scorecards.
- Avoid off-limits questions; focus on skills and context.
- Provide candidates clear timelines and role context.

Offer components:
- Base salary, equity grant (level-based), benefits, and applicable signing bonus.
- Compensation bands are accessible to hiring managers via People-ops.

4) Onboarding: first 90 days (detailed checklist)

Day 0–6
- Welcome email from People-ops, equipment shipment, and SSO invite (Okta).
- Complete HR forms and tax/benefits enrollment (if applicable).

Week 1:
- New hire orientation (company mission, org overview) and team intro.
- Manager 1:1 to agree first 30/60/90 goals.
- Access request submitted and verified (GitHub, Jira, Confluence).
- Complete security awareness training.

Month 1:
- Merge first small contribution and attend codebase walkthrough.
- Join paired programming and shadowing sessions.
- Meet cross-functional partners (SRE, Product, CS).

Month 2:
- Begin owning a small feature or improvement with clear deliverables.
- Present a 30–60 day plan in the team sync.

Month 3:
- Formal 90-day checkpoint with manager and mentor; update career development plan.

Onboarding contacts and roles:
- People-ops onboarding team: onboarding@redwood.com (ticket for missing access).
- Manager: responsible for role-specific ramp and goal setting.
- Buddy: assigned for social and tactical questions for 90 days.

5) Benefits & perks (quick reference)

Health & financial:
- Medical, dental, vision plans with HSA options. Coverage typically effective from the first day of the month following the start date.
- Retirement plan with employer match.
- Equity grants at hire and periodic refreshes aligned to performance cycles.

Time off & leave:
- Flexible PTO policy (recommendation: at least 15 days per year).
- Parental leave: primary 16 weeks paid, secondary 8 weeks paid.
- Sick leave and caregiver leave per local regulations and company policy.

Perks & allowances:
- One-time home office stipend: $1,200.
- Learning stipend: $1,000/yr.
- Wellness reimbursements and meditation subscription.
- Annual company retreat covered by Redwood for travel and lodging.

How to get help with benefits:
- benefits@redwood.com or file a ticket in the People-ops Jira project (PEOPLE-OPS).

6) Internal tools & access (quickstart + owners)

Essential tooling and default owners:
- Slack: workspace access via Okta; EngOps manages team channels.
- Okta: SSO and MFA; self-service guide in /confluence/eng-infra/okta-setup.
- GitHub: "redwood-inference" org; repo access requested in onboarding form.
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions + internal runners; see /confluence/eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build.
- Jira: project keys ENG, PLT, INFRA, PEOPLE; managers create boards.
- Confluence: documentation workspace and templates for RFCs, runbooks, and postmortems.
- Monitoring: Datadog (metrics) and Sentry (errors); SRE adds engineers to alerting rotations.
- Secrets: Vault + KMS; elevated access requires security approval and training.

Access provisioning workflow:
1. New hire submits Access Request Form (People-ops onboarding checklist).
2. Manager approves and specifies repos/projects.
3. EngOps provisions standard accounts within 1-2 business days.
4. For production or admin privileges: complete security training and submit a privileged access request to security@redwood.com.

Recommended first-week engineering checklist:
- Clone and run the quickstart repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/quickstart.git.
- Join team on-call shadowing.
- Request read-only production logs and metrics access.

7) FAQ, escalation points, and governance

Common questions:
- Payroll or benefits issues: payroll@redwood.com or People-ops Jira.
- Start a hiring requisition: create a req in Greenhouse and obtain manager + finance approval.
- Find role rubrics and interview guides: /confluence/company-handbook/roles-and-career-ladders.

Escalation contacts:
- People-ops lead: Avery Chen (people-ops@redwood.com).
- Head of Engineering: Priya Desai (eng-head@redwood.com).
- Security: security@redwood.com.

Governance & update process:
- Document owner: People-ops. Review cadence: annual or after major policy/vendor changes.
- To propose edits: open a Confluence edit request and tag People-ops plus one reviewer from the reviewers list.

Appendix A — Promotion packet checklist
- One-page impact summary with key metrics and outcomes.
- 3-5 supporting artifacts (PRs, design docs, runbooks).
- Peer feedback (3+ peers) and manager endorsement.
- Updated career development plan and proposed new scope.

Appendix B — Useful links & templates
- Onboarding checklist template: /confluence/company-handbook/onboarding-checklist-template
- Promotion packet template: /confluence/company-handbook/promotion-packet-template
- Interview rubric: /confluence/company-handbook/interview-guidelines
- Okta setup guide: /confluence/eng-infra/okta-setup

End of guide. For corrections or questions contact People-ops (people-ops@redwood.com).
